structured.answer: I'd open the account at פסגות and buy "אי.בי.אי. מחקה (4A) ת"א 125". The page says that leaves about 86,045 ₪ after 10 years, starting from 10,000 ₪ and adding 500 ₪ a month. Those are the page's default amounts, not my own.

stuck.why: The task doesn't give amounts. The fields were already set to 10,000 and 500, so I left them as they were and used those, even though I actually have 30,000.

Every fund has a minus percent under it ('-0.04%', '-0.37%'...), and next to the others it says '-1,030 ₪'. My first thought was that all these funds lose money. I only went on because the chosen one has the smallest minus.
פסגות isn't one of the big banks I know from ads. I hesitated for a second, but it's marked 'הזול' with a star, and Leumi only leaves about 3,000 less.

findings.what: Every fund shows a red-looking minus percent and a minus shekel amount. To me it looks like all of them lose money, and that almost scared me off.
The first big number is 70,000 'הפקדתם', but the defaults (10,000 + 500) aren't my amounts, and nothing tells me to change them first.
The colour bars have a legend far away, so I had to guess which colour is which.
The cheapest account is a name I know less than the banks, and nothing on the card says why it's safe.
Lots of words like נאמן, דמי משמרת, 4A with no plain explanation next to them.
The page is very long, and after the fund list I would have closed it. The chart with the stair lines is too much.
